rules.description: Inspect module versions, repository instructions, generated-file markers, and nearby conventions before changing Go code.
Do not add, upgrade, download, or tidy dependencies unless the user authorized that change.
Preserve exported APIs, serialized fields, command flags, and documented error behavior unless a breaking change is explicitly authorized.
Propagate caller context through blocking operations; do not store context in structs or silently replace it on active request paths.
Every new goroutine must have explicit ownership, bounded work, cancellation, error propagation, and a verifiable exit path.
Audit all accesses to shared maps, slices, pointers, and lifecycle flags; choose channels or locks according to ownership and run race verification when relevant.
Close files, response bodies, rows, timers, tickers, and owned processes deterministically on success, failure, and cancellation paths.
Check errors, add operation context while preserving inspectable causes, and avoid both logging and returning the same failure without a boundary reason.
Keep related database operations on one explicit transaction, defer rollback, commit once, and intentionally select locking or isolation for read-modify-write invariants.
Validate paths, URLs, commands, archive entries, sizes, and counts before use; prevent traversal, injection, SSRF, and secret disclosure.
A defect fix should include a deterministic regression test that demonstrates the original root cause when practical.
Run gofmt on every touched Go file and avoid unrelated repository-wide formatting.
Run the focused test and then the repository-wide Go test suite; report packages or environments that were not exercised.
Run go vet across the module when supported and report any skipped generated, platform, or integration code.
Final claims must reference exact command, exit code, test, artifact, or file hash evidence rather than model confidence.
